subject: MSA + Order Form: remedy-tiering & liability cap — IP indemnity carve-out?
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Clarke <daniel.clarke@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: remedy-tiering & liability cap — IP indemnity carve-out?

Hi Daniel / Margaret / Sasha,

Thanks again for taking time on the call yesterday. We reviewed the MSA redlines your legal team sent on 7/12 and had a few follow-ups specifically around the liability cap and the carve-out you added for IP indemnity/remedies. We want to propose language that protects Aurelia (reasonable IP remedies) while keeping Redwood's commercial exposure predictable for operational risk modeling.

Quick summary of our position:
- Redwood can accept an IP-indemnity exception to the liability cap limited to direct costs for defense + final awards tied to a confirmed infringement finding, but we cannot accept an uncapped obligation for speculative consequential categories or open-ended injunctive liabilities without narrowing language.
- If you need injunctive relief language for design-around obligations, we ask for a mutual mitigation step (60-day cure/repair period or negotiated escrow) before injunctive remedies kick in.
- For third-party patent claims we proposed a capped statutory remedy bucket that preserves indemnity but limits non-monetary obligations.

Attached: a marked-up MSA and a short IP_Claims_Table that maps potential claimant scenarios to proposed remedies.

Can your legal team review the three alternative clauses we highlighted (A: full carve-out with mitigation timeline, B: capped compensatory carve-out for IP awards only, C: mutual injunctive framework + escrow) and let us know which is closest to acceptable? If helpful, we can supply a redline that implements option B.

Next steps: if you confirm which option you prefer, I’ll coordinate a legal-to-legal exchange and loop in Contract Ops for order-form sequencing.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0178

Attachments: Aurelia_MSA_redline_20260712.docx (MSA redline), IP_Claims_Table.csv (scenario mapping)

From: Margaret Li <margaret.li@aureliatx.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Daniel Clarke <daniel.clarke@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Sasha Nguyen <sasha.nguyen@aureliatx.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: remedy-tiering & liability cap — IP indemnity carve-out?

Naomi,

Appreciate the clear summary. Aurelia legal is OK in principle with narrowing the scope, but we need to preserve a carve-out that: (i) excludes the IP indemnity from the monetary cap; (ii) allows equitable relief (injunctions) where monetary damages are inadequate; and (iii) keeps Redwood responsible for third-party IP claims it indemnifies.

Two asks from our side:
1) We cannot accept a waiting period before seeking injunctive relief in the event of ongoing infringement impacting patient safety or regulatory compliance.
2) We want to ensure any cap on IP awards does not penalize Aurelia where Redwood's modifications / future model changes generate new exposure.

I'm attaching Aurelia's short counter-language. We can be flexible on exact phrasing but need clarity on the carve-out's scope vs types of damages excluded (direct vs consequential).

- Margaret
Margaret Li
Sr. Counsel, Aurelia Therapeutics
margaret.li@aureliatx.com

Attachment: Aurelia_MSA_IP_counter_20260714.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: remedy-tiering & liability cap — IP indemnity carve-out?

Looping in Rafael from Legal Ops — Rafael, please see Aurelia's asks below. Two operationally important points for negotiation:
1) If we leave injunctive remedies unlimited, we need a narrow carve-in that ties injunctive obligations to a court adjudication or a mutual technical remediation plan tied to a severity threshold.
2) For the Order Form, pricing needs to reflect residual exposure if we accept a broad IP carve-out (i.e., premium / escrow / liability insurance). Please advise on fallback collar language: either a defined monetary bucket for IP awards (e.g., 5x monthly recurring revenue up to $X) or a requirement that Aurelia maintain IP-specific insurance.

I drafted a short fallback clause we can propose; Naomi, can you surface that to the customer and ask whether they prefer an injunctive exception only for regulatory/patient-safety issues vs. for any IP claim?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Operations
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Margaret Li <margaret.li@aureliatx.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: remedy-tiering & liability cap — IP indemnity carve-out?

Margaret / Aurelia team — thanks for the quick reply. A few concrete suggestions from Redwood Legal based on common market practice: 
- Keep IP indemnity carve-out from the monetary cap for reasonable defense costs and final awards, but explicitly exclude consequential categories (lost profits, business interruption, speculative punitive damages) from the carve-out unless court-awarded and directly tied to the underlying infringement judgment.
- Permit equitable relief but require that injunctive remedies be conditioned on an emergency standard (e.g., TRO or court order) OR, alternatively, that the parties first engage in an expedited tech remediation protocol for 14 days where a material compliance/regulatory impact is asserted. This preserves emergency relief for safety/regulatory while avoiding open-ended operational obligations.
- If Aurelia insists on no timing gates for injunctions, we need a contract-level mitigation: either an escrow to cover injunctive compliance costs or an express insurance requirement.

I've prepared three redline paragraphs (attached) mapping these options and a suggested Order Form premium line item that compensates for an uncapped injunctive exposure. Happy to discuss on a short call.

-Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_IP_carve_options_20260715.docx

From: Daniel Clarke <daniel.clarke@aureliatx.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Margaret Li <margaret.li@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Sasha Nguyen <sasha.nguyen@aureliatx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: remedy-tiering & liability cap — IP indemnity carve-out?

Team — thanks for the options. Aurelia's commercial team discussed and we are inclined toward Redwood's Option B (capped compensatory carve-out) but with two caveats:
1) We need injunctive relief available immediately for alleged infringements that could impact regulatory filings — can't wait for a TRO in those cases.
2) For the cap mechanics, we prefer a sliding-tier that relates to annual committed spend rather than a fixed flat number (helps align to contract value as the deployment scales).

Sasha offered to coordinate a short call next week to finalize whether the sliding-tier formula or an insurance requirement is the binding fallback. Can Naomi set 30 minutes?

Best,
Daniel
Director, Strategic Ops, Aurelia Therapeutics

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Clarke <daniel.clarke@aureliatx.com>, Sasha Nguyen <sasha.nguyen@aureliatx.com>
Cc: Margaret Li <margaret.li@aureliatx.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: remedy-tiering & liability cap — IP indemnity carve-out?

All — calendared: Tues 7/27 10:00am PT (30m) — invite sent.

Prep notes for the call (summary):
- Aurelia prefers Option B (capped IP carve-out tied to contract value), Redwood preferred emergency injunctive carve-in for safety/regulatory with remediation protocol for non-emergency.
- Agenda: finalize whether sliding-tier formula or insurance obligation will sit in the Order Form; agree injunctive trigger carve-out language; confirm whether Order Form price band will change if Aurelia rejects the insurance requirement.
- Action items: Rafael to circulate the 3 redline paragraphs + short sample sliding-tier formula by EOD Mon 7/26; Naomi to confirm attendees on Aurelia side and share Order Form v3 draft; Karthik to prepare suggested pricing collars for Commercial.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Naomi
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
